questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good university, a place within the EU, a place to meet new people from different cultures

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have made many new connections with people, which has really been an enriching experience. However, the courses and school has been very demanding and difficult.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy enough.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were help to get both at university campus and dorm campus. However, I did not use it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They did not have enough spaces at orientation, tour, etc. for all exchange students, which I found very weird. You had to sign up way in advance to get a spot.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Mostly just dorm rooms in different places in the city. I chose one close to my host university.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: At my dorm, we had a shared kitchen with the necessary utilities – however, there was no oven.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: PLEASE CLEAN UP AFTER YOURSELF!!!!! A lot of people do not leave the facilities nice and clean, and it is extremely disrespectful to your flatmates.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can register online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I do not know, help was not necessary. However, there was a pretty thorough description of the process on VU's website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I succesfully got enrolled into all my chosen courses. I did not have any issues.
If I wanted to change workgroup, this was sometimes also possible, even after the course had started.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it in advance! I was a little late with officially registering for courses, which did end up becoming a bit of a stress factor.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The courses have overall been interesting, but they required quite a lot of work. More so than I am used to from UCPH, and you should be aware of this in advance. 
Also, they do not have many breaks. I did not have a week off until Christmas break.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were more difficult than expected.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style is quite similar, lectures and workgroups/tutorials (øvelsestimer). However, there were much more to prepare, and I had more assignments during the semester here. Also, the exam was not the only thing that counted for the final grade, assignments, attendance, etc. were also included. Additonally, all exams were closed-book exams, meaning you do not have any aid at all during the exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I took a minor called "Sustainability: Management and Innovation".
It consisted of the five following courses:
• Grand Challenges for Sustainability, 6 ECTS-points
• Shared Value Creation, 6 ECTS-points
• Organizing Sustainable Innovation, 6 ECTS-points
• Sustainable Business Processes, 6 ECTS-points
• Marketing Sustainable Innovations, 6 ECTS-points

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I can personally recommend Grand Challenges of Sustainability and Marketing Sustainable Innovations.
I found these the most interesting, and the others I did not necessariliy care about.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My computer broke, so I had to pay for the reparation. Insurance covered most, but I had to pay the self-risk.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Alcohol is cheaper than expected (especially wine at the grocery store).
Public transport is more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really attend any. But they did throw a good start-of-semester party in the beginning.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a sport and cultural center. They also have student organizations you could join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sport centre is a good place to attend classes or go to fitness, and it was on my dorm's campus which made it very easy to go.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The museums here are great (personally I recommend Straat, Fabrique des Lumieres, Stedelijk, and van Gogh), and they have some cute cafés! Also, the canals and Vondelpark are a great place to go for a walk. And I personally fell in love with the area called Jordaan.
Haarlemmerstraat (close to the central station) has some very nice secondhand shops that I often frequented.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The Dutch culture is pretty similar to Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really, it was very hard actually meeting Dutch people here. I did make a few Dutch friends, but that was because we took some of the same courses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I am used to a biking culture, however, people here bike without much discipline. They do not stop for pedestrians at cross walks, signal when taking a turn or similar. They bie as if they own the city, so be aware of that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People here are in general much more open. They greet you and smile if you make eye contact, which is really nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Go to as many social event in the beginning as possible! It really helps you network and get a social circle!

2. Of course you have to spend time studying, but also prioritize exploring Amsterdam and other cities close by! Enjoy that you are not in Denmark! However, please attend the lectures, they sometimes will provide information that's in the curriculum but you may not find online (in Canvas) otherwise!!

3. Remember to prioritize yourself! You will have a lot of new experiences here, which can be very enriching but also overwhelming. So taking time for yourself every once in a while is necessary.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people and connections that I have met here. I know that I have made friends for life because of this experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To manage the study load with the social life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
